thread:
sara: hitting a warmup regression on canary: large safetensors bundles with 256KB micro-shards are stalling at step 2 (verify) ~12% of the time under spotty WAN. leads to full-shard fallback and a 4x warmup blowup. :confused:
max: is this the compact-stream loader or the mmap path?
sara: compact-stream. looks like missing trailing bytes on a small fraction of requests. tends to be first-reader on a shard after cold-start.
liang: hypothesis: we validate only per-shard checksum. with micro-shards we should validate per-microblock and have a cheaper repair path than re-fetching whole shard.
priyaa: what do you mean by "cheaper repair"? small-range re-download?
max: yes — store byte-level parity blocks in the manifest. if block N mismatches, request parity delta for that block (XOR parity or small erasure piece) and heal locally. saves bytes compared to re-getting the whole 200MB shard.
sara: tradeoffs: extra manifest size and encoding complexity, but manifest can be gzipped and parity blocks are tiny relative to whole shard. also need to consider encrypted private deployments (KMS keying for parity chunks).
liang: interface idea: extend weightsource manifest with optional `micro_parity` array:
```
manifest: {
  shards: [...],
  micro_parity: [ { shard_id, block_offset, length, parity_uri, algo: "xor-v1" } ]
}
```
Client flow: 1) stream micro-block -> compute running_hash, 2) on mismatch -> GET parity_uri, 3) apply xor to heal, 4) re-verify block hash, 5) publish atomically.
priyaa: need auth semantics: parity_uri should accept the same signed token as shard GETs and return signed parity metadata. add `parity_scope` to KMS policy if needed.
max: atomic publish: write micro-block to ephemeral path `shardX.blockY.tmp` then Fs.rename -> `shardX.blockY`. also create `shardX.blockY.lck` lease during write so readers wait or fallback. avoids partial reads.
sara: eviction races are nasty here. if eviction removes shard directory while we're healing, we need a safe retry: acquire global shard lease or abort and let top-level hotfill restart.
liang: simpler: short-circuit eviction when `inflight` marker present. eviction checks `inflight` TTL and skips until TTL expires to avoid tearing. put TTL conservative: 30s.
max: metrics: counters for `micro_heal_requests`, `micro_heal_success_bytes_saved`, `micro_heal_fail_fallbacks`. tag by region, client_type (hosted/dedicated/private), and transport.
priyaa: we should also track `manifest_parity_coverage_pct` so we know how many models publish parity and performance impact.
sara: perf estimation: for our canary model, average parity delta is 64KB per repair vs 200MB full fetch -> ~3000x bandwidth savings on repair path. but compute cost is small (XOR).
liang: one more: backwards compatibility. if `micro_parity` absent, loader falls back to exact current behavior (whole-shard re-fetch). keep feature-gated server-side to avoid new clients mis-reading.
max: plan: 1) server-side: manifest schema bump + endpoints for parity_uri; 2) client: implement ephemeral write + lease + xor-heal + metrics; 3) canary via feature-flag `micro_parity_heal=true` rolled to 10% of nodes; 4) run chaosnet with 1-5% packet loss for 48h and compare warmup tail latencies.
runtime-bot: canary rollout scheduled: build 2026.03.21-microheal-01, featureflag=eng-ml.micro_parity_heal@10pct.
priyaa: also add a security review for parity URIs in private deployments - parity endpoint must never return unwrapped plaintext without KMS check.
sara: i'll implement loader-side POC and a small manifest generator. will post numbers once chaos runs finish. thx team. :rocket:
